utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-99-36-T, The Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language which you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can follow in a language which I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you, ma'am. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here with David Cunningham and Aleksandar Vujic, back in my more familiar spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to you, too. Yes, I see you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's only a question of the timetable for, effectively, the rest of the evidence. Your Honours are calling the witness this morning. I don't know whether Your Honours can give us a rough idea how long you're going to be with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, we are going to follow the same procedure we did last time. We have prepared -- one moment. We have prepared a list of questions which I am going to put to the witness. And then as we go along, as one question might breed another, then obviously there might be questions coming from either Judge Janu or Judge Taya or even myself in addition to what we have here. I don't anticipate much more to be frank with you. I reckon we should definitely be well over with this witness by the first break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, Your Honour -- again, as we don't know what Your Honours are going to ask, we don't know yet from our side how long we'll be. Can I just inquire whether Your Honours got a copy of a document. It had already been a part of an exhibit, but we found a translation for it, and we handed it -- Mr. Ackerman, I think, had it. It was the order from Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's available.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are -- we have the Teslic Binder, folder, yeah. So we've prepared ourselves obviously with all the documents that we thought would be necessary or might be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But beyond that I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was merely inquiring because we made arrangements to get it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That document we do have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, then the next matter is this: As Your Honour knows, I have objections to a number of the exhibits that Mr. Ackerman wants to put in, and he has given us an added one this morning to which I also object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which added one?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I ask Your Honour doesn't read out the name, please, in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that before Mr. Ackerman formally closes his case, Your Honour will have to deal with that. The question is if there isn't sufficient time today, are Your Honours going to sit on Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On Monday, Ms. Korner and Mr. Ackerman, I was -- is Mr. Roberts here? No, he's not. I was in contact with Mr. Roberts this morning through email, internal email, asking him to contact you and Mr. Ackerman with a view to possibly holding a meeting on Monday to discuss the business we are going to have together next month. So I was suggesting 11.00, subject to both of you being able to be present and subject, of course, because at the time I had not yet spoken to Judge Janu and Judge Taya about the time. But we have other business to discuss on Monday, so I imagine that I could go ahead and ask Mr. Roberts to contact you. I suppose since you're saying this, you haven't been contacted as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But my intention is to have a meeting with you, that's the three of us with you and Mr. Roberts, and maybe someone else on Monday at about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly that's convenient for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's convenient. Obviously, if that's not convenient, we can talk of Tuesday. We have a witness on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We do. And Your Honour, that's why I was saying -- that witness won't take very long, I don't think, but as I say, I think we need to deal with the objections to the exhibits before Mr. Ackerman formally closes the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, definitely. What I suggest is that since we have not discussed the matter at any length in camera amongst ourselves, that we leave this matter outstanding until Tuesday, and we will decide it on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Also, we need to make sure which documents you are referring to and that we have got a complete picture. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to your suggested meeting, I wonder if it would be acceptable if we could do it like immediately after the sitting on Tuesday so that I don't have to make two trips down here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, Tuesday the position is as follows,

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I personally have no problem at all. The only thing is this: I imagine that -- Tuesday, we are sitting in the afternoon, Madam Registrar, no? I do not anticipate that particular witness who is coming over to testify on Tuesday to be here for more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't -- there's cross-examination. The witness may only be half an hour in chief, but there's cross-examination as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that witness is testifying on one particular instance -- all right, make it one hour. But that gets us to 3 -- let's say it takes us to 3.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour needs, I think to hear the argument on the exhibits first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- before the witness is called because it's a witness in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's -- then the meeting, I suppose, won't last more than an hour. The only thing is I need to be at the airport as I explained to you last time sometime in the evening. My wife returns that day at 7-something, I think. So I need to go and pick her up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise, she won't return again, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that kind of attitude, Your Honour. Your Honour, my objections to the Prosecution's exhibits were all given to you in writing, and that saved a lot of argument time in Court. It would seem to me if Ms. Korner could simply give you the objections in writing, that we could shorten this up rather dramatically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Really, I think this is a question for oral discussion rather than in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. It's not the end of the world. We can cope with that. So would you agree to, therefore, postpone the meeting on the other matter until Tuesday --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm perfectly happy with that. I would suggest that we hold it sometime in the morning, as Mr. Ackerman will have to come on Tuesday in any event, rather than after court on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It makes no difference to me. I'm really at your disposal. I can come any time you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will now need to discuss with Mr. Roberts, my legal officer, to see what commitments he has, because the entire next week Mr. Von Hebel will not be here, so practically he will be responsible for the whole team. And I don't want to tax him unduly. So I'll come back to you later on today directly or indirectly through Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was told by Mr. Ackerman that some of the exhibits I've objected to, he may not be seeking now to put in. So perhaps if he could let me know, that would also shorten matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will do that right now. It will take me a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, I want to formally offer and tender Defence exhibits 1 through 379 with the following exceptions: I wish to withdraw Exhibits 77, 90, 91, 92, and 342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not much, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's more than the Prosecution has withdrawn, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, the Prosecution has failed to tender thousands of documents, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could have tendered something like a hundred thousand pages had I felt inclined to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm glad you didn't, Ms. Korner, because the -- our office -- the sooner I get rid of this case the better. I'm just looking forward to seeing all those binders leave my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was told actually by Ms. Hollis, that the original intent - she's one of the original people who came here - the original intention was this should be a paperless Tribunal, and it's never worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In my country, I was in charge, way back in the 1980s, of the computerisation programme, and before that I embarked on that I went to the States and I went to England to see. The States were much more advanced at the time, England not yet. I remember some of the courts, particularly in Slough, for example. I went to see how it was operating, et cetera, and I convinced myself we were going to get more paper than we were actually used to. And I carried out the whole computerisation programme over the years, believe me, you start printing out yourself plus you're given hard copies, plus you get drafts and drafts and drafts. And it's impossible. Anyway, let's bring the witness in. Does he -- he hasn't asked for any protective measures, has he? To my knowledge, no. Where is he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this Tribunal. You have been summoned to appear, give testimony in this trial against Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin by the Trial Chamber itself. I suppose you are already familiar with the procedure. If not, tell me and I will explain to you. But the first thing that you ought to know is that before we can proceed with your testimony, our Rules require that you make a solemn declaration to the effect that in the course of your testimony you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. You are a judge, so you know exactly the importance of this declaration. You have the text of the declaration in your hands. Please proceed. Read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you state your name and surname, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Goran Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in 1955, in Doboj, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your ethnicity is Serb?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you give us some information on your education.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the faculty of law in 1978. And since then, I have worked in the justice department throughout. I worked as a judge. That was up until 1976 [as interpreted]. And from 1986 onwards, I worked as the basic public prosecutor in Doboj. From mid-July 1992, I worked as the president of the high court in Doboj. From 1994, I worked as assistant minister for justice. And in 1998 -- since 1998, I have been working as a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there must be a mistake. Because it says he worked -- he graduated in 1978. But it says on the transcript: "I worked as a judge up until 1976." It must be 1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, is it correct you graduated in 1978? Yes, I don't see the --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I said I graduated in 1978. And that since then, I worked in the judiciary including my charge at the higher prosecution office. From 1998 [as interpreted] to 1986 I was also working as a judge. In that period of time, I also did my military service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I heard from the headphones 1998 until ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clear this. I will put a direct question straight away. After graduating -- you graduated from which university?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Faculty of law in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you worked as a judge up until which year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: From 1981 to 1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. From 1981 until 1986, okay. And then from 1986 you worked as a public prosecutor, and then subsequently as a judge, as a president of the high court in Doboj. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what was your position in 1992 when you say you became president of the Doboj court in July, mid-July 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: From the 10th to the 15th of July, I was the charge d'affaires of the president of the high court in Doboj because the elections had not gone through yet, had not been completed. That is de facto when I started working. On the 20th of July 1992, I was elected, together with other judges, as president of the high court, and official authorisation from the Ministry of Defence to work in the court I received on the 1st of August. Which means from the 1st of July between the 10th and the 15th, I was already working as the president of the high court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As president of the high court, I don't know how your system works, did you report to anyone? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. A high-court judge was in charge of solving cases sent up by the lower courts, first-instance courts. The high court, however, was duty-bound to send in his report to the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Justice sends it on to the national assembly for adoption. Of course, if the court is not working properly, then the Ministry of Justice can ask the national assembly to relieve him of his duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you had no direct superior, did you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just before and until you became president of the high court in Doboj, were you still performing duties as a prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, although I was listed as working, and I did receive a salary from the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what you were actually engaged in? What kind of work were you engaged in?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I was the acting president of the high court. That is to say, I represented the high court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you actually start working as the acting president of the high court? Which day? Which date?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until the 10th of July 1992, what was your position?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Public prosecutor in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And as public prosecutor in Doboj, who was your direct superior?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The higher prosecutor in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was he? Or she?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: His name was Mr. Stevan Savic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if I read you well, you became -- you were appointed president of the Doboj court, high court, from your position as prosecutor, public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who appointed you as president of the Doboj high court?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The Judges' collegiate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the Judge's collegiate --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I apologise. Not the collegium. They did not appoint me. They put me forward, nominated me, and then put forward that proposal to the minister of justice for the president of the court and the judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So all the incumbent judges did not choose a president from amongst themselves, but they chose someone from the prosecution, the public prosecutor for that matter, and that was their recommendation to the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Prior to your coming here to the courtroom to testify today, have you spoken to anyone about your being summoned to give testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to my family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: But not about the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I just want to make sure that I am right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Today, you are no longer occupying a public office. You are in private practice. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In your life, were you ever a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not even the communist party or whatever it was called in your --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I do apologise. I was a member of the communist party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you cease being a member of the communist party, League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1990, when it was dissolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in other words, even when you were still a judge, because you told us that there was a time until 1986 that you were working as a judge, you still held a membership card with the League of Communists at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. All judges were members of the League of Communists. They couldn't have held a post otherwise. A person who was not a member of the League of Communists could not become a judge or hold a public office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Were you a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. In 1990, there were instructions banning people in public office or banning judges from being members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, let's come to the most substantial part of your testimony or the reason why you are here, in particular. I am going to refer you to the events that took place allegedly in Teslic and which involved a group known or called as the Mice group. Have you ever heard of such a group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the circumstances that led to the Mice group coming or arriving in Teslic? Do you know how come they got there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know how they arrived, but while I was still working in the prosecutors' office, I learned that in Teslic, there had been a conflict between the police from Doboj and the police from Banja Luka. And that a group of people had been arrested and that they were being detained in Teslic. Later on, I learned about this case from the documents, the documents before you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you were aware of the arrival -- at the time, of the arrival of the Mice group in Teslic before you learned that they had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no. I learned about them only when they were arrested. As follows from this criminal report, they arrived in Teslic in two groups. One group arrived on the 3rd of June, and the second one on the 6th of June. They were arrested on the 30th of June 1992. On the 8th of July, the police submitted a criminal report against them; that is, against a total of 16 persons. The police said that eight of them were members of the Mice, seven were civilian policemen and the rest were soldiers. It was a total of 16 persons. On the 10th, the prosecutor submitted a motion for an investigation to the Teslic court asking for them to be interviewed, for witnesses to be interviewed, and to have it checked with the military and police command whether these persons belonged to their units. On the 10th of July, the investigating judge of the court in Teslic issued a decision on initiating an investigation against these persons. Five of them confessed. They were charged with depriving various people of their freedom in illegal ways, serious theft, extortion. Five persons from the army also confessed. The others did not. On the 16th of July, the investigating judge and the president of the court in Teslic informed me, as the president of the court, that in the meantime three persons had been released because there were no further grounds for keeping them in detention and that 13 persons had been transferred to the district prison in Banja Luka. It was not clear to him why they were transferred there. On the 17th of July, I wrote a letter to the president of the district court in Banja Luka, to the Ministry of Justice, and informed them that these persons were to be held in detention in Doboj because Teslic was within the jurisdiction of the high court in Doboj, and the appropriate detention unit was in Doboj. Two or three days later, these persons were transferred from Banja Luka to Doboj. I do not know about the manner of their transfer. This was done in Banja Luka, and they were already in the district prison on the 21st of July. The investigating judge in Teslic, on the 21st of July, again released eight persons, and the reasons he gave was that they had been interviewed, that witnesses had been interviewed, that there were no further grounds for detention, and that the military command had requested that these persons, as soldiers, be sent back to the fighting so that only five persons remained in detention as of the 21st of July 1992. They remained in detention until the 6th of August. On the 6th of August, the investigating judge moved that the five of them, that their detention be extended. The accused submitted a complaint, and then these five were also released with the reasons they had been interviewed, that witnesses had been interviewed, that they would not influence each other, and that if the previous group had been released on the 21st, there was no longer any reason to keep these men in detention. And that is all of the Mice were released from detention on the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the way you have explained these events, it seems to indicate that you had absolutely nothing to do with this whole process, except that you wrote this letter on the 17th of July --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to have the detainees transferred from Banja Luka to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I wrote this letter on the 17th of July and delivered it to the president of the district court in Banja Luka, to the Ministry of Justice, and I think to the district prison. I have a copy here. And on the same day, it says in the upper right-hand corner "A/A" and my signature, because I felt that the case was closed, that I had done my legal duty. I may be wrong or I may be not. But it was accepted that I was right to do this. The person in charge of the entire proceedings was Nenad Kovacevic, the investigating judge, who knows all the details of the case. What I have told you I said on the basis of the documentation at my disposal, which I read before this session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- On that note may I raise something. I note that the witness has a very large file in front of him. Your Honours may not be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I saw him entering with a binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know how Your Honours would want to deal with it, but I would request that before I cross-examine I be allowed to look through the file. And because I can't read the language, I'm going to ask for one of the language assistants to go through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what did you bring with you by way of documents? I saw you entering with a green folder or binder.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a copy here of the Official Gazettes which the Prosecutor also has. For example, about the jurisdiction of the high court. This is the Official Gazette of the 17th of May. Then there is the decision on the election of myself as the president of the court. Then there is my letter of the 17th of July which I addressed to the high court in Banja Luka. The criminal report of the 10th of July. The motion to institute an investigation of the 10th of July. On the 11th of July, the decision to conduct an investigation. The Prosecutor has this also. Then here I have two requests sent to the court, and this is cut out from the newspapers, from the military command, and from the police, that they be released. On the 21st of July, there is the decision ending their detention. And another such decision dated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the date.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: These are the documents I obtained in 1999 because that was when certain articles were published about this group, and my name was mentioned in this context. That's why I wanted to have this documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How come you know -- or you tell us that you know which documents the Prosecution already has?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I know because this decision on conducting an investigation which I have has the markings of the Prosecution. I borrowed this from another case because I was involved in another case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is -- I was going to raise this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He must have acquired these documents as a result of being Defence counsel for Mr. Krajisnik. Unless he's still employed on that case, those documents should have been returned to the new counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I wanted to know first and foremost how he knows what you have and what you don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was going to raise exactly the same question. But it didn't occur to me this was the only way --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It's only one decision. The other documents are not from that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I leave that until the end of the evidence. I want to raise that issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously, yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Were you ever asked to make a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the events related to the Mice and their release?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody asked me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, who -- again, could I have you repeat the name of the investigating judge in Teslic that took all these decisions.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the investigating judge in Teslic that took all the decisions that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Nenad Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was his position in the hierarchy in the court in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The president of the court and an investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And as a judge and president -- he was president of the court of first instance, I'm informed.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So as president of the court of first instance, who was he directly answerable to? Who was his direct superior?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He was independent in his work. He was directly responsible to the Ministry of Justice, as all courts were, both first instance and second instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there a court of second instance in Teslic? Was there a high court?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The second-instance court was the high court I worked in. That was the appellate court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he answerable to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Under the law, he could not be answerable. We at that time only dealt with appeals against decisions issued by the first-instance courts. Every court reported to the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Justice compiled a report for the assembly evaluating the work of each court. He was appointed like me by the assembly and could be dismissed by the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, page 15, line 3 of your testimony of today, you testified: "On the 16th of July" - now, this is when you are already president of the Doboj high court - "the investigating judge and president of the court in Teslic informed me as president of the court that in the meantime three persons had been released because there were no further grounds for keeping them in detention and that 13 persons had been transferred to the district prison in Banja Luka." Why would the investigating judge and president, I suppose we're talking of the same person, Mr. Kovacevic, why would the investigating judge have to inform you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Because this was already a regional issue by then. The detainees, had they been transferred within Doboj, he wouldn't have had to inform me. But as they were transferred to the area covered by another court, then he had to inform me of this. It was just information. Because it was a conflict of jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you inquire with Mr. Kovacevic why they had been transferred to Banja Luka and -- why they had been transferred to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he only informed me that the police from Banja Luka had taken the detainees from Teslic to the prison of Banja Luka. I think he did this because there was a conflict between the Banja Luka police and the Doboj police. Up to the moment of the arrest, as far as I know, Teslic was under the control of the Doboj police, the Security Services Centre there. After the arrest, Teslic was controlled by the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. That's how it remained throughout the war. Now again it is under the control of the Doboj Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why do you say "after the arrest, Teslic was controlled by Banja Luka security services"? Am I right -- or rather, I put it to you that Doboj or the Municipality of Teslic -- sorry, the Municipality of Teslic, by a declaration of the 4th of April 1992, joined the Autonomous Region of Krajina with Banja Luka being the capital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to correct, I think it's the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, probably you're right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this decision on joining the Krajina. I know that up to the outbreak of war, Teslic belonged to the Doboj region and was under the competence of the Doboj Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did the war start?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The war started in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So why do you say that after the arrest, Teslic was controlled by Banja Luka security services? Because if the war started in May, and you say that up to the breaking of the war -- breaking out of the war Teslic did not form part of the Banja Luka, that's a contradiction. So basically what I'm suggesting, you are fully aware, according to what you testified, up until July of 1992 when you were president of the Doboj high court, Teslic was already part or controlled by the Banja Luka security services and not by those in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That could be. I am not an expert on this. But I do know that before the war, Teslic was within the area covered by the Doboj Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The war had already -- the war had already been on for a couple of months at least, and the president of the Doboj high court, I would expect to be familiar with who was actually controlling what and from where before getting involved in matters of jurisdiction between municipalities and before issuing the order to which you referred earlier on in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. But according to the decision, the Teslic court is under the jurisdiction of the Doboj higher court. It was never under Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But before involving yourself in this, did you try to find out how come and why these persons forming part of the Mice group had been transferred to Banja Luka? Who had ordered their transfer to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The president said only the police from Banja Luka. That was the only information I had. The police from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But let's speak now in legal terms because you are a judge, and therefore you should be in a position to give me these answers. Once a person is detained, charged and detained, does he or she fall within the jurisdiction of the court or not, in your country? Who can decide on his state of detention, on his condition of detention? Who has got jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems that these detainees were transferred -- were they transferred by the judge? Or were they just transferred by the security services or by the police or the military to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think the judge did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So why didn't the judge refer the matter straight to you before we had a fait accompli, before these detainees were transferred.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He informed me on the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could Mr. Kovacevic have stopped their transfer to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he could have. I conclude this because after studying these documents I see that they were detained on the 30th of June. And the criminal report was submitted only on the 8th of July. This means that they were detained without any court decision for the first eight days of their detention. The first court decision on this was issued on the 10th of July. On the 30th -- that's right, the dates were 30th June, 8 July, and 10th July, and that's why I conclude he could not have prevented it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just clarify, is the witness saying 13th or 30th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, are you saying 13th, 1-3, or 30th, 3-0, June?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you're saying that when they were transferred to Banja Luka, they were not yet formally under the jurisdiction of the court in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I don't know when they were transferred to Banja Luka. Yes, yes, I only said that they were arrested on the 30th of June, and that from the criminal report I see that it was submitted only on the 8th of July. The president informed me on the 16th or 17th, I think. It's in my letter. Yes, on the 17th, I learned that these persons were transferred. On the 17th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you try and investigate why and who had -- why they had been transferred to Banja Luka and who had issued the order for their transfer to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I assumed it was the police from Banja Luka. That's what the president told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you try to verify why, how come that Banja Luka security services had claimed for themselves these detainees and had them Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. transferred from the Teslic jurisdiction to the Banja Luka jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. However, I just heard that the Doboj security centre filed a criminal report against the members of the police force from Banja Luka to the Teslic prosecutors' office because they considered them to have acted unlawfully, but I don't have that particular report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the time all this was happening, were you aware or had you been put -- made aware of the kind of activities that the Mice group had been engaged in in Teslic prior to their arrest?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Only what it says in the documents, that there were murders, that it concerned looting, extortion, and they were deprived of their freedom against the law. And it also says that those individuals represented themselves falsely to be soldiers and policemen and that they acted as a parapolice force and paramilitary. And that is why the public prosecutor in his request for an investigation asked the investigating judge to check out with the police and army whether they were, in fact, paramilitaries and parapolicemen. From the report by the investigating judge dated the 21st of July, we can see that he released eight persons who were soldiers, and the reasons I have already said was that they were questioned and interrogated and that the military command asked these individuals to be released. So the military command, thereby, recognised that they were indeed military men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you aware or made aware of the circumstances under which the Mice group were arrested?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I did have some knowledge about that. I wasn't working at the high court at the time, though. But there was an armed struggle, I was told, between them and the police from Banja Luka and that two policemen were killed on the occasion, and that a number of other policemen were wounded. And that that's how they came to be arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why would the police of Ban -- from Banja Luka be involved in this, in this operation of the arrest of the Mice group if you maintain that it was the Doboj security service and Teslic security -- or Teslic police that were responsible?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But didn't it occur to you --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that's -- I think it was a question of who would be in charge of Teslic because as I was informed at that time, the head -- the chief of police in Doboj was in Teslic and that he was beaten up, up there. Those were the rumours going round. But anyway, Teslic was cut off from Doboj, so it was very difficult to communicate with it and nobody went to Teslic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean, "nobody went to Teslic"? What do you mean to tell us by that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what I meant was people didn't go on a daily basis. There were no telephone lines, no electricity. If you received some information, you would receive it through courier in a period -- during a period of seven days or seven days' later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was the chief of police that was beaten -- allegedly beaten up in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Andrija Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was the chief of police in Teslic at the time of the arrest of the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In Teslic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Teslic, yes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was Dusan Kuzmanovic, but I'm not quite sure. However, I think it was Dusan Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the commander of the police station? Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. No, I don't. I wasn't in Teslic, so... And the komandir would be a lower level post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would it be Predrag Markocevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a man called Predrag Markocevic who did work in the police in Teslic. I don't know what position he occupied, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that almost immediately following the release of the Mice group, Dusan Kuzmanovic was replaced by someone else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who was appointed. I know he was replaced. But who was appointed in his place, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he replaced by Predrag Radulovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I know Predrag Radulovic. He's a colleague of mine. He's a lawyer. But I don't think he was appointed as chief of police, although I'm not quite sure. I think Predrag Radulovic was -- worked at the Banja Luka police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is precisely what I'm suggesting to you, that Dusan Kuzmanovic was replaced by Predrag Radulovic as a consequence, as a result of an ad hoc order from Stojan Zupljanin. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that Predrag Markocevic, who was, I suggest to you, commander of the police station in Teslic, immediately after the Mice release was replaced again as a result of a direct order from Stojan Zupljanin by a certain Milenko Savic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't even know who Milenko Savic is. I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the time all this was going on, and particularly on or around the date the 17th of July when you wrote that order, where you sent that order to have the Mice group returned to Teslic or Doboj Municipality, were you contacted by anyone on the matter? Did you speak to anyone on the matter, apart from Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody contacted me, either from Banja Luka or the Ministry. Nobody did, nor from the police. I don't remember anybody contacting me about that. And it wasn't an order, it was just a letter to a colleague of mine of the same rank as myself. As far as I can see here, I placed the letter and dated it after I -- I put it A/A, case closed, in the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were the members of the Mice group or any of them linked to a superior authority? Let's start from here. Are you aware that some of them were members of the military?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. From the criminal report one can see that nine individuals were members of the army, and seven were members of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically, they were all under superior authority.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From your investigations in these -- on these matters, are you aware of any representations made by the military with regard to those members of the Mice group that were members of the military? You have already stated earlier on in your testimony that there was a specific request by the military command to have them returned to barracks so that they could fight. But are you aware of this through your own investigations or through reports that you have read or you may have read?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I learned about it on the basis of the report, where the military command is asking for that and where the judge, the investigating judge from Teslic, states in his report that that was being requested of him by the military command. Now, whether the army undertook anything with respect to those individuals or not, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware -- I mean, I know that 14 years have -- almost 14 years have practically passed from those events, but are you aware if any action was taken by the military with regard to those members of the Mice group who were also part of the military?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you tried to find out?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not investigate that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What happened to these members of the Mice group after that they were returned from Banja Luka? Were any of them at any time subjected to a trial, to trial proceedings? Were any one of them tried?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: They were under investigation. And as far as I know, the investigations ended in 1993, and there was something else that needed to be done and that was the exhumation of the persons killed and that then the president of the investigating team asked resources for the exhumation. But as there were no resources for that, the case remained open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: So that an indictment was never actually raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are aware that an indictment was never actually made against any of the members of the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: There are certain proceedings underway at the cantonal court in Zenica in the Federation. Now, for what cases, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But for all intents and purposes, are all the members of the Mice group still at large, walking around as free men?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume they're walking around as free men, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any reason why the military, for instance, or the police or the security services for that matter, because as you said, nine of them were members of the military, seven were members of the police, are you aware of any reason at all why the military or the police would not have been aware at the time of the reasons why the members of the Mice group were arrested in the first place and of the details of the alleged -- of the crimes alleged to have been committed by them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think the army and the police knew the crimes they were alleged to have committed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why, in your opinion, do you think the members of the Mice group were transferred to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think the reason was because it was the police and military from Doboj. I think that was the main reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean? My question was why in your opinion were the members of the Mice group were transferred to Banja Luka. And you're telling me the reason because it was the police and military from Doboj. I don't really understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume -- it was like this. The police in Banja Luka was in conflict with the police in Doboj. So that means there were people who were wounded, injured, killed. And they decided to have them transferred to Banja Luka because they didn't dare bring them to Doboj because there was this conflict. And nobody at the time went to Teslic or went from Teslic to Doboj. There was a conflict going on. So I think that was the main reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did Banja Luka security services have a right, according to you, at the time to have them transferred to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. If they were under the court's jurisdiction, they did not. All they did have was to keep them in detention for three days, a maximum of three days. Now, if the judge made a decision, then they would have to be in the detention unit in the place where the high court is, and the high court being in charge of the lower court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if, as I suggested to you, starting from the 6th of April of 1992 it was the Banja Luka security services that had jurisdiction in that area, wouldn't it make sense to you that the Banja Luka security services had every right at the time to have them transferred straight away to Banja Luka, rather than have them kept and detained in Teslic? Wouldn't that make sense to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it would not make sense, Your Honour. They can keep somebody for only three days, either in Teslic or Banja Luka. Now, if there is a court order by the judge pertaining to detention, then they would have to be at the detention unit in Doboj because the order made by Teslic with respect to the centre of the police has nothing to do with jurisdiction. The judiciary, which was in keeping with the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You told you don't really know whether they were already under the jurisdiction of court or not at the time they were transferred. So why did you get involved?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Because the president of the basic court informed me that he had already released three men from detention, so it was under his authority, and that the police had transferred the rest to Banja Luka. That is point 2 or paragraph 2 of my letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that brings me back to the question that I asked you earlier: How would and why would a responsible judge, the president of court, allow the transfer of detainees who are under his jurisdiction when he shouldn't?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think they even asked him that. I don't know how this actually happened, but I don't think they asked him. And he didn't inform me that he had -- why would he have informed me if he hadn't had this problem in the first place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, you're suggesting that they were transferred to Banja Luka without the judge being consulted or informed, without Mr. Kovacevic being put into the picture?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I can only assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were not consulted as president of the high court in Doboj, were you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, you did tell us earlier on, according to how the -- according to the documents that you were referring to, why and when the various members of the Mice group were released. Could we go through that again in greater detail. I want to know exactly what happened step by step, who was released, before who and after whom, and who released them and what was the reason.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, yes. This is how it was: On the 9th of July 1992, a criminal report was brought in against 16 individuals, 9 individuals belonging to the army and 7 belonging to the police. The 8 individuals who were in the army were called "the Mice," as the criminal report says. May I take a moment, please, to look through the documents. On the 16th of July 1992, detention was revoked against three individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Those three individuals, were they members of the police or were they members of the army? These are the first three individuals that are released.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. One was a member of the police, two were members of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the reason for their release?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't got a document about that. I was just orally informed by the president of the basic court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: And the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But did the president, President Kovacevic, tell you why he had ordered the release of those three individuals.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think he said there were no grounds for proceedings against them because allegedly they weren't there throughout that period but just happened to be there by chance on that night when they were arrested, but I'm not quite sure because I don't actually have the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have the names?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I have written them down here. Slobodan Karagic, Zoran Tadic, and Predrag Subotic. And I named them in my letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the next batch of --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 20th. The investigating judge in Teslic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when were they returned from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Around the 20th or 21st. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So they were returned on the 20th. And what happened on the 20th now in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, you were about to tell us "then on the 20th" -- I had asked you when was the next batch, next group released. And you mentioned the date of the 20th.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The 21st. I apologise. It was actually the 21st. And I started reading out the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of July 1992, the investigating judge revokes detention for the following persons, eight individuals: Sljivic Rodoljub, Sljuka Ranko, Sljuka Zoran, Slajuvica Dario, Mimic Ranko, Gavranovic Sasa, Kezunovic Dragomir, and Devic Vitomir. That is the military group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that counts how many?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: 11. And then it says: "Reasons by the judge: The investigating judge finds that by interrogating the individuals and a certain number of witnesses, basic investigatory work has been conducted, and most of the people questioned owned up to having committed the crimes. And pursuant to the law, this Court finds that with respect to the individuals mentioned above, there are no further reasons for detention being effective. And the time and circumstances have shown that they were military men and that the individuals will be subjected to the military command and will, therefore, not influence other witnesses who have not yet been questioned." Those are the reasons stated by the judge. The judge was Nenad Kovacevic, and the date was the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. There is a part of the transcript which I don't understand. Perhaps I could ask you to read out again the first sentence of that paragraph. The investigating judge finds that by interrogating --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you read slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. "The investigating judge finds that after interviewing the accused and a certain number of witnesses, the most necessary investigating actions have been performed, and most persons confessed to having carried out crimes, committed crimes," and then there is a list of the legal provisions. According to the provisions of Article 190, Article 3 of the Law on Criminal Procedure and provisions of Article 191, paragraph 2, items 2 and 4 of the above law, this Court finds that in relation to the above-mentioned persons, there are no longer any reasons for detention." The judge has especially taken account the request of the above-mentioned military command the time and the circumstance that these are military personnel and are carrying out the most necessary investigating actions, finds that they will be subjected to the control of the above-mentioned military command and will therefore not be able to influence witnesses who have not yet been interviewed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So at this point in time after the release of this next group, are there any other Mice group members still being detained?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What happened to those five?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of August 1992, these five accused complained, or rather appealled against their detention, and the file reached the Doboj high court where three judges reviewing criminal cases, Drago Stokic [phoen] as the president, Savo Lehovic [phoen], and Lazarevic Miroslav, as members of the panel, issued a decision, handed down a decision approving Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the appeal of the appellants and changing the decision of the Teslic court and abolishing their detention. The prosecutor of the high court in Doboj has in writing submitted a motion to take into consideration the appeal of the accused. In the statement of reasons, it says the following: "The court of first instance has interviewed a large number of witnesses in these criminal proceedings and has, therefore, completed the most necessary investigation of the accused. In the decision of the 21st of July" - so this Court refers to the previous decision - "the other accused had their detention revoked. Therefore, there are no special circumstances indicating that the accused will interfere with the investigation by influencing witnesses. Furthermore, there is no evidence to show that the actions of the accused have disturbed citizens, and further it is not of evident that detention is necessary in order to further conduct the criminal investigation. For this reason, the court finds that the grounds of appeal are justified and, therefore, the court overturns the decision of the court of first instance and orders that the detainees being released." And that's how they were all released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask that I be given, at this stage, the witness's file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, we're going to join in the request to look at the file as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, unless he's got some personal papers of his that might not be related --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to see any documents that he has with him that relate to this, the evidence he is giving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge, could I ask you to make that file available both to the Prosecutor and to Defence counsel, please. Thank you. We'll have -- then perhaps we can have a longer break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we'll have to because I'm going to ask our language assistant to go through that with me now, and then I'll give them over to Mr. Cunningham. If I can have them for the first 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Your Honour were to say instead of 25 minutes, 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm at your disposal, Ms. Korner, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That will give us both a chance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know how you're going to go about this. But are you removing papers from that file?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He is, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why are you removing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why are you separating some papers from others? What are you actually doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to take out the documents connected with my testimony. Well, that's not all. I have here a brochure with information for witnesses at the Tribunal. This is not -- I'm just taking out the relevant documents, relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But let us decide what is relevant and what's not. I suggest you leave everything there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then obviously you will have everything back. Thank you. We will rise now, a 40-minute break. If you require more, just let us know and we are at your disposal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In your country at the time, before and after, someone who is charged with murder, especially multiple murders, who confesses in the course of the investigations conducted by the investigating judge, was it normal procedure, has it ever been normal procedure, that that person is practically immediately released a few days after the confession? Or do you find this utterly abnormal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Utterly abnormal. Usually, in cases of multiple murder, or even ordinary murder, the person is usually held in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So didn't it strike you as very abnormal to have on the 21st of July eight persons who, according to the investigating judge most of whom had confessed to the crimes imputed to them, to be immediately released? Didn't that strike you as very abnormal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: To be quite honest, up to that -- I got this decision in the archives and read it only recently. But I think it is unusual to release people if there is evidence that they committed the above-mentioned crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they were released by the same Kuzmanovic, no? Kovacevic, sorry. Dusan --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Nenad Kovacevic, investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They were released by the same Nenad Kovacevic, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to look, Your Honour. I think that in that decision, it says that this was at the proposal of the public prosecutor. Usually they're held in detention if the public prosecutor opposes their release. If the public prosecutor agrees with their release, in most such cases the court approves the release, although the court is not bound to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, let's go back a little bit before I return you to this part of your testimony. The ones who were released on the 21st of July by Judge Kovacevic, were they all members of the military?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say that in the decision. And in the criminal report, it says that yes, they were. They were members of the military. I only wanted to add in connection with this decision, I found it when they were released, it says here the public prosecutor in Teslic agrees that the accused be released. That's the decision concerning the persons you are now asking me about, dated the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Doesn't it strike you as strange in the least that they are returned from Banja Luka on the 20th, allegedly interviewed between then, after that, all of them, I suppose, and released the day after? Doesn't it strike you as very strange that the day after their return the judge who until their transfer to Banja Luka had no reason to release them effectively releases them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The judge handed down the decision on the 21st of July 1992. This decision reached the prison on the 24th of July, as there was no postal service or telephone. And it says here, released on the 24th of July 1992 at 15.10 hours. I think that the -- there was a three-day delay. I think that when the judge released these persons, that he took into consideration the request by the military command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But doesn't that make you think that the return from Banja Luka to Doboj or to Teslic was not just a matter of jurisdiction, but a carefully planned strategy to be able to satisfy the requests of the military in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was a strategy. To be sure, I cannot speak on behalf of the investigating judge. I don't know whether he had any talks with the military. Nobody applied to me to have them released. As for the army, it was all one. The 1st Krajina Corps covered both Doboj and Teslic. They had a single command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You addressed your letter of the 17th July to the president of the Banja Luka high court. That's Jovo Rosic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he at any time contact you on the -- on this letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you try to contact him before sending the letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, there were no telephone lines. If you look at my letter, it was sent by telefax. It's something like Morse code. The telephone lines were down. I didn't contact him or the ministry because the lines were down, nor did they contact me. Simply three days later I learned that the detainees had been transferred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness please be shown Exhibit Number P1938. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember ever having seen it before. I see that this is addressed to the prosecutors' office. No, no, the prosecutors' office was independent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what does this -- what is actually this document? What does it purport to be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: This document is information on instituting criminal proceedings against members of the military police and the Security Services Centre in Doboj, and problems relating the actions of judicial organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you haven't -- you have never seen it before, you say?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't recall ever having seen it before. I see here on page 4 that my name is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you to read, please, for yourself or read out aloud paragraph 10 on page 4 of the document.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I would like the interpreters, rather than referring to the document, to the translated document in English that we already have, to follow the reading by the witness himself and try to translate as he goes along. It's not a long paragraph. I want to make sure that the translation -- that the translated version of the document that we have is correct. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the 20th of July 1992," --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness read slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neskovic, Judge Neskovic, could you read slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the 20th of July 1992, from the head of the criminal service of the public security station in Teslic, the public prosecutor and investigating judge learned that all the accused were released from the district prison in Banja Luka and that they are at large. Not doubting the information from the Teslic -- from Teslic, the public prosecutor" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "And at the president of the higher court's office, Jovo Rosic, that the warden of the prison in Banja Luka, without his knowledge and approval, pursuant to a telex from the president of the high court in Doboj, Goran Neskovic, released all the detained persons because of whose taking over the district prison in Doboj. The president of the high court in Banja Luka showed us the teletext in which the president of the high court in Doboj asks the transfer of the detainees to the district prison in Doboj as the one with jurisdiction of place. Unofficially we learned that the arrival of these persons in Doboj was celebrated in front of the public security station and that all the persons were released."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are your comments on this paragraph? Because it seems to me that the investigating judge himself is pretty much surprised that these persons are released and returned back -- released and returned back from Banja Luka, while it doesn't seem to be the case in Doboj where according to this report there were even celebrations in the CSB building?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this. I know that while they were in detention, the investigating judge, Nenad Kovacevic, and the public prosecutor visited them in Doboj, and that then they dropped in to see me. I remember that. I don't know that anybody celebrated anything. That I sent a telex, that's true. And the president of the court knew about the telex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How do you know that the president of the court knew about the telex if this reports states --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He received it. Rosic. He got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This report maintains that the Mice detainees were all released without his knowledge and approval, and that there was already a vehicle from the Doboj district prison ready there to collect them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's a slight confusion here. He's talking about Rosic, and you're talking about Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, I'm talking about Rosic. What paragraph 10 states is that according to Rosic, these Mice detainees were released without his knowledge and approval and that there was already a bus from Doboj waiting for them when they were actually released. Do you have reason -- yes -- do you have reason to doubt what your counterpart in Banja Luka supposedly stated to the persons who drew up this report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Are you saying that Rosic said that these persons had already been released in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I am saying that according to this report Jovo Rosic informed the persons who prepared this report that the Mice group were released from the Banja Luka prison without his knowledge and without his approval.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Transferred, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And there was a Doboj district prison bus waiting for them as well.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't go to Banja Luka, and I don't know that. How it came about that they were transferred from Banja Luka to Doboj, I don't know. I think it was the prison wardens in agreement with Rosic who determined the logistics of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rosic is saying he never gave his approval and he didn't even know that they had been released. And I want to know from you who would have sent the Doboj district prison bus to collect these detainees from Banja Luka. Not you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Who in Doboj can decide what's done in Banja Luka? Only the president of the high court. Somebody has to give the order to the prison in Banja Luka and say "I approve that these detainees be transferred to Doboj." Or "I don't approve." Doboj can't do that. No chance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What this paragraph states is not what you are stating, Mr. Neskovic. What this paragraph is stating is that these persons were released without the knowledge of high court president Mr. Rosic, without his approval, and when they were released there was a Doboj district prison bus waiting for them.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: This happened in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it happened in Banja Luka, yes, as a result of your telex.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
