utterances.text: No, no. I only sent a telex to the president of the court in Banja Luka, the Ministry of Justice, and the district prison. I did not contact anyone, nor do I know how they were released or who gave the order for their release. That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it so happens that the Doboj district prison bus was there to pick them up precisely when they were released. So someone must have been informed -- someone must have been informed in Doboj. Someone must have been informed in Doboj about their imminent release.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I help on this -- if the witness -- if Your Honour goes to the document that he's talking about, the telex, and you look at the last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it says that they will be sending a bus.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It says in the telex. I sent a telex to the president of the court, and it says: "On the 18th of July we shall transport the detainees. As you are in charge of the detainees, if you have any problems in connection with this, please advise us by telefax through the Ministry of the Interior."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But they were not transferred on the 18th; they were transferred on the 20th, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: So somebody agreed, bypassing the presidents of the court about this, but somebody in Banja Luka had to give their approval for the release on the 20th. I asked for the 18th. They didn't come on the 18th. I didn't send any other letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you inquire what happened on the 18th after you did not see the Mice group back in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did the prison van go to Banja Luka and return without the prisoners on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think this was agreed on at the level of the prison wardens. The prison wardens discussed among themselves how they would do this if they got approval. I put A/A, the 17th, on my document, archiving it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you try to contact Mr. Jovic to see why the 18th had passed and these detainees had not been handed over to the prison van which had been sent from Doboj? Did you at least inquire to see what happened?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you check on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't check anything, except for sending this fax, and it was only three days later that I learned that they had arrived. I didn't expect them to arrive. They could have left and not arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rather, these 16 members of the Mice group, am I right in saying that they were -- am I right in saying that the ones which were -- who were members of the military were all military policemen from Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that offhand. I think most of them were. But I think it says here, gives their names, where they come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Just one wasn't from Doboj. He was from Teslic, number 16. He is registered militarily in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, who was the one? Was it Captain Petrivcevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't registered. He's not on the criminal report. As far as I knew, he was also arrested and was somewhere in military detention. Now, who conducted those proceedings against him, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he, in actual fact, the head of the group inside the Mice group that were members of the military? Was he in command of that particular part of the group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. All I know is that he was a Captain Petrivcevic who was not from Doboj, a native of Doboj, his first name was Ljubisa, and that he was incarcerated in the military prison in Banja Luka. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other members of the Mice group, I put it to you that they were group members of the security services in Doboj. Is that correct? And that Milan Savic was responsible for that component part of the Mice group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Seven members of the police is how many there were. As to Milan Savic, he was the deputy chief of the security centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically we're saying that out of these 16 members of the Mice group, 15 were certainly from Doboj. Only one seemed not to be from Doboj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what it appears to be from the criminal report. Number 16, born in Teslic. I don't know where he resided. Perhaps he resided in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I put it to you earlier that Dusan Kuzmanovic was replaced by Mr. Zupljanin following the release of the Mice group. And you agreed to that, although you could not agree or you could not confirm that he had been replaced by Predrag Radulovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I know Predrag Radulovic. As to the rest of it, I don't know about that. I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that Dusan Kuzmanovic was a member of the crisis staff of Teslic at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I know Dusan Kuzmanovic because he went to the gymnasium, to school with me in Doboj. That's why I remember him. And I know that he was chief of the public security station in Teslic. But who the members of the crisis staff in Teslic were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown, please, Exhibit Number 2438, please. 2438.1. Or 2438 anyway. Yes, if you have the -- if I am given a copy in B/C/S of the document I can refer the witness immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: It's 7 on the B/C/S. Page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please go to page 7 of the document. Go to page 7 of the document, halfway down the page, there's the name Dusan Kuzmanovic. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see Dusan Kuzmanovic on page 7 anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have the document here, please, for a moment. This is in English. I want the B/C/S. That's why he wouldn't -- couldn't find it. Yes, could I ask you to read that paragraph which -- first of all, what document do we have -- are you looking at?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: This is -- well, I don't know what this document actually is. There is a statement of reasons of some kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Look at the first page of the document, first paragraph. What does the title state?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that this is an extract from the notes of the 18th regular meeting of the municipal assembly of Teslic held on the 20th of August 1992 in the hall of the municipal building of Teslic. So these are the minutes from one of the municipal assembly meetings, and it states the agenda. Now what this actually means is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go to page 7 on that document. And could I ask you, please to, read out aloud what Mr. Kuzmanovic is reported to have stated in the course of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Dusan Kuzmanovic says that "the observation made by R. Jokic that in Teslic" - and it says that the Mices appeared as a military formation - "does not stand, is not true. The group had official authorisation from the superior military command for conducting mobilisation and establishing civilian power and authority in the municipality, and the protagonists wielding power and authority have been informed of that. All the activities of the public security station of Teslic were under the patronage of the crisis staff. As regards the activities of this operational group, the crisis staff was informed thereof, and the police had the role of leader in these activities. The conflict with the operative group in Doboj occurred at the point in time when the mentioned criminal took part."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can read the last sentence of that paragraph again because the translation -- interpretation did not come through complete. "The conflict," please read the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "The conflict with the operative group from Doboj occurred when the mentioned crime in which allegedly the political peaks of Teslic took part."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what does that --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "Mention was made of the crime in question."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What does that all mean to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: From this observation, it would appear that there had been some conflict with the operative group from Doboj on the part of the authorities in Teslic, because some crime was mentioned. A conflict with the operative group from Doboj occurred when this crime occurred, and then it says: "Participation of the leadership in Teslic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it seem clear to you that the Mice group had the blessing and the protection of the highest authorities, political, civil, and military, from the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's how it would seem, judging by the observation made by Kuzmanovic, the head of the station, the chief, that they had official authorisation from the superior military command to conduct mobilisation and establish civilian authority in the municipality, and that all the protagonists of the leading posts in Teslic were aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And doesn't it occur to you that the fact that these people are still at large and no real trials took place against them in essence means that that protection has never ceased?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The president of the court in Teslic wanted to complete the investigation by 1993. However, he didn't have the resources necessary to exhume the victims. And I think that he was in conflict with the authorities in Teslic to a certain extent. And I think that in 1994 actually, they accused certain functionaries in Teslic of having committed crimes, as far as I remember. Now, Mr. Kovacevic would be best placed to tell you about that, to tell you what his relationship was to the official authorities in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the Doboj Court of Appeal did reverse the decision of Kovacevic not to release the remaining five Mice members still detained, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that fell within the jurisdiction of your court. You are responsible for that court, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I was the president of that high court. However, to be quite frank, nobody could wield an influence of those judges. They made their decisions themselves, and the reason for that was the public prosecutor had proposed that the detention be revoked. And once you get a proposal from the public prosecutor, then in 90 per cent of the cases the court agrees to the proposal made by the public prosecutor. And they said that if the -- on the 21st of July they were released, then why should the others remain in detention? If they were taken into custody for the same reasons, you can't hold one lot and release another. That is how I understand this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It could also be understood that what Mr. Kovacevic left undone, the Doboj high court completed. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. That is not so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is the result -- is the ultimate result of the decision of the Doboj high court that all the members of the Mice group at the end of the day following that decision were free and at large?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, just five individuals. The high court gave orders for the release of just five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were it not for the decision of the Doboj high court, there would still be five individuals detained? Is it solely because of the decision of the Doboj court that those five individuals were also released, leading to all the members of the Mice group released?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were at large.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I'm suggesting to you that what Kovacevic left incomplete your court made sure to complete.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. He completed their release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I put it to you also, sir, that the reason why you insisted upon the return of the Mice group from Banja Luka had nothing to do with jurisdiction but had absolutely and completely to do with ensuring that military and police from Doboj were brought back to Doboj to be released immediately after.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. My intentions were just to act in accordance with the law at that point in time. And the detainees who were transferred to Doboj would remain under the competency and authority of the investigating judge from Teslic. And had they stayed in Banja Luka, the investigating judge could have released them on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that in Teslic the release of the Mice group was considered very negatively and is still considered very negatively to date?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware that it was considered negative. Depending on who said what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown again, please, Exhibit 1938. This is once more the public prosecutor in Teslic writing to the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of the Interior, and Ministry of National Defence. Could I ask you to read out aloud paragraph 11, which is the penultimate paragraph in that document, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: "The arrival of the group from Doboj and the written authorisation by the command of the operative group of Doboj, the organisation of the group by the leaders from the area, Kapetan Ljubisa, and the civilian authorities, deputy chief of the public security centre of Doboj, the manner in which they have worked, their conduct, the command of the operative group after their arrest and release, the detainees from the district court in Banja Luka, without the knowledge and acquiescence of the judge in the basic court in are, the facts which, with the staff of the judiciary and all the citizens of Teslic, are creating justified doubt in the work of the organs and military bodies in Doboj. And this leads to the conclusion that a state authority has absorbed among its ranks people of little knowledge and doubtful morals which leads to crime, and this is a dangerous link between political authority and the underground which could inflict great damages to the Serbian People and state unless the necessary measures are taken forthwith to stop this. For the above-stated reasons, I consider that this piece of information should be sent out to the competent authorities of the Serbian Republic of BiH so that within the frameworks of their lawful undertakings they should investigate the case and bring the culprits to justice, undertake necessary measures to prosecute the culprits."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say on this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what do you want me to say? How can I react whether I see that the prosecutor wrote that on the 28th of July 1992, whereas the same man on the 21st proposed that eight individuals be released from detention? That means that he was doing one thing and writing another. And I have -- I was not aware of this piece of information, but I agree that the conclusions made therein are the right ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who do you think he's referring when he says: "State authorities had taken into their ranks people of scant knowledge and dubious morals from the past"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably he means the police that were mobilised into the police force and the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Janu is also referring you to another part of the same paragraph -- in the same paragraph where it states that "the dangerous connection between the political authorities and the underworld could cause enormous damage to the Serbian People and the state unless the necessary measures are promptly taken." Again, what is the prosecutor, public prosecutor referring to? What kind of dangerous connection between the political authorities and the underworld could he be referring to here, according to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to me, he is -- if he refers to political authorities, he probably means political authorities in Teslic. And when he refers to the underworld, he probably considers that to be the units who were in the army and the police as being that underworld.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's move. I ask you, sir, do you have any political pressure brought to bear on you when you decided to send that letter on the 17th of July? And if you prefer not to answer that question, just ask me not to answer it. I find it very hard to believe from what we know about the events that you wrote that genuinely out of your anxiety to preserve jurisdictional rights of the Doboj court. I find it difficult how a president of the high court in Doboj in something like this does not contact first the -- his counterpart in Banja Luka, discuss the matter, and agree on how to proceed. I find it difficult that the president of the Doboj high court writes a letter in which he specifies exactly the time and date when the prison bus will pick up the detainees, these detainees are not picked up on the specified date and time, and the president of the Doboj high court does not query that. And when we have a report which states that ultimately these persons were indeed released without the knowledge of the president of the Banja Luka high court, and without his consent, of course, but when they were released the prison van was there, the prison van sent from Doboj. I find it difficult to believe that in all this you acted out of your determination to protect the jurisdictional rights of the Doboj Municipality.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've already stated that I didn't occupy the post of the president of the high court from the 10th to the 15th of July. I did not know Mr. Rosic, nor had I ever seen him before in my life. So this was quite a new post. That's the first point. Now, if you're talking about peacetime, the high court is 2 kilometres away from the front line during the war, and 30 to 40 shells hit the court building daily. So we weren't working eight hours a day. We would work one hour on one particular day or not work for several days. Judges would come in for work or they would not. What we're talking about was a war situation, but nobody exerted any pressure on me ever, and I stand by that. I did so in the interests of justice on my own, have those detainees in detention, and then I asked Mr. Rosic to have them transferred. I wasn't able to contact him because there was just one telephone line that was open in the information centre, and I wasn't able to access that telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You still haven't answered my question. Was Mr. Kovacevic in favour of their being returned from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic just informed me that they had been transported to Banja Luka. And having been apprised of that, that's what I wrote in my letter. I don't think he knew about the telex. He was only informed of it once the telex reached Banja Luka. Now, who released them, I don't know. I certainly could not have released anybody in Banja Luka, nor could I have gone to Banja Luka at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him in 1992. I think I got to know him in 1994 or 1995. Mr. Trbojevic introduced us, my colleague -- a colleague of mine who is an attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's his name, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Milan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he Minister of Justice at one time in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think he was never the Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the vice-president or the deputy prime minister in 1992. But not the Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware whether he was an attorney representing someone before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Milan Trbojevic? Oh, yes. Mr. Brdjanin. It was on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when did you meet Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1994. I think he was an attorney then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And was he in the company of Mr. Brdjanin when you met Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall. I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with Mr. Trbojevic or Mr. Brdjanin the events in Teslic relating to the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember ever having discussed it with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the events in Teslic and the Mice group with anyone from the military in Teslic or in Banja Luka, anyone from the 1st Krajina Corps, later the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Neither in 1992 nor later did anyone contact me or ask me anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the arrest of the Mice group with Predrag Radulovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Predrag Radulovic and I see each other very often, but I don't think we discussed this. We may have done, but I can't recall. We are colleagues, and we are in touch every month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the events about the Mice group and their release in particular with Milenko Savic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who Milenko Savic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With Milan Savic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I know Milan, but I -- oh, yes. I think I did have a conversation with him, but that was at a later date, not at that time. Milan Savic lives in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And what was the gist of the conversation with Milan Savic on the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: This conversation may have taken place in 1999. An article was published in the newspapers about the Mice group in which I was described as a traitor because I was a liaison officer and the person who had given information to the international prosecutor here. That was the context of our conversation. Four articles were published in a period of four weeks about this case, and these documents were published. But nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss these matters, the Mice -- related to the Mice group with Colonel Stevilovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know this colonel. I never met Colonel Stevilovic. I think he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before he got killed, did he ever contact you on the Mice --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Stojan Zupljanin? Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: About the Mice? No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with Jovo Rosic --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour. I didn't even know that Teslic belonged to Banja Luka. I thought that Teslic belonged to Doboj, so I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. never had any conversations with Banja Luka, nor did I ever go to Banja Luka to discuss this matter with anyone. I never even discussed it later on with Jovo Rosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And before I pass you on to the other Judges, who was the most influential and the most powerful person in Teslic at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think the president of the municipality then was Nikola Peric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think he --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He was the president of the municipality, yes, and he nominated judges and prosecutors on behalf of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he wield the real power, or was it just a post that he held without indeed wielding the real power?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I wasn't in Teslic in 1992. I know that later he was replaced, sometime in 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Doboj, who was the most powerful person in 1992 when these events took place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of police. That was Andrija Bjelosevic. He was the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not the mayor, not the president of the municipality, in other words?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. The president of the municipality was Mr. Drago Ljubicic. He was the president of the municipality, but I'm referring to the area of Teslic. And that was Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in Doboj, who was the most --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In the municipality, the president of the municipality was Drago Ljubicic, and the president of the executive board was Mr. Paravac [phoen]. And the two of them were the highest government authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But who really wielded the power in Doboj at the time? Who decided things? Because we have heard several instances of presidents being there as a front and nothing else, and the power being wielded by others. Who wielded the power in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I think they all made decisions together, the president of the municipality, the president of the executive board. There were deputies. There were three or four deputies from Doboj, Mladenko Vasiljevic [phoen], Mr. Jaudic [phoen], Milan Ninkovic, and I don't know if there was a fourth. The army was there, the 1st Krajina Corps, Milivoje Simic was there. He was a colonel. Later on, it was General Lisica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What about the crisis staffs? Did they have any power?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That was a municipal body, and they only made decisions relating to the municipality. I don't know enough about that because the judiciary was not under the authority of the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that in several municipalities in Bosnian Krajina, several judges were removed as a result of decisions taken by the crisis staff of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. As for the Autonomous Region of Krajina, I don't know because I wasn't there. Doboj did not belong to the ARK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Doboj was a separate region, before the war, during the war, and after the war. The organisation has remained the same throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With regard to Banja Luka, can you tell us who wielded the power in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can only tell you what I saw in the media. I didn't go to Banja Luka. I didn't have contacts with anyone from the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what did the media tell you about who wielded the power in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw General Talic as the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps. I saw Predrag Radic as the president of the municipality. I saw Stojan Zupljanin as the chief of police. I saw Mr. Brdjanin on several occasions. I think he appeared on television, too. And that was it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think for the time being I've finished with my questions. Judge Janu, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Not at this stage. I will ask some questions at the closing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Taya.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Mice group terrorised all population of Teslic after their arrival. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Was it not true that everyone in Teslic knew Mice after their arrival?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the manner of their arrival. I only got to know about them when proceedings were instituted against them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: After the release of 16 members of the Mice group, weren't there any incidents by those men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think there is some difficulty with the transcript, if I could ask you to repeat the question, Judge Taya.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Okay. I repeat my question. After the release of 16 members, all the members of Mice group, weren't there any incidents by those men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidents, yeah. Were there further incidents after their release in which the Mice group were involved that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear of any incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Didn't they take part afterward in war operations with the aim of breaking the military resistance of Islamic fundamentalists?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't in the army. I don't know anything about the army or the police. I remained working in the judiciary. I assume that they had to be part of military units and that they fought against the other army because they could not remain unmobilised. They had to be part of military formations of some sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: I stop my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. There are no further questions from the Bench for the moment. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I say, I'm not going to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will move on to Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just so the witness also knows. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you make preparations for your return the end of this week, Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the Registry --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Registrar will make sure that he is given all the assistance he requires to change the ticket and whatever. Yes, Ms. Korner, you can --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is intending to take a break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have been sitting for an hour and 15 minutes roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So about quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we will finish at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is there going to be a break between now and a quarter to 2.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think there ought to be. Because we can't sit for another hour and ten minutes without a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If I stop at 20 minutes to 1.00, Your Honour is going to have a sort of 15, 20-minute break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Questioned by Ms. Korner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, you've told us you're friendly with Mr. Radulovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that not only have no proceedings ever been taken to indict the Mice, but the Mice or members thereof have been suing Mr. Radulovic, taking him to court?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: A criminal report was filed against Mr. Radulovic in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, recently in the last couple of years, are you aware --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, yes. He told me about it, that he's involved in legal proceedings, but I don't think it relates to that. I think it's something else. He didn't tell me the details, but he said that he was engaged in a civil suit with two members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the Mice?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct. Radulovic told me about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reality, isn't it, that nobody in Republika Srpska from 1992 until 2004 has made any proper attempts to prosecute these murderers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Or a statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you a question. That's the truth, isn't it? That's the reality?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That they were not prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody has --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: They were prosecuted, but the proceedings have not been completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Twelve years after the event? Is that what you're telling us, Mr. Neskovic, 12 years after the event there has been no opportunity to complete the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not for me to decide about this. I left in 1998. I left the judiciary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a matter for the public prosecutor when proceedings will be initiated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to some of the problems of this prosecution in a moment. But I want to put, if I may, the Court a little bit in the picture of Doboj. Doboj in 1992 was a municipality --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm looking at P60 now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that contained something in the -- well, exactly according to the 1991 census 41.000 Muslims who constituted 40 per cent of the population. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the statistics, but probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 39.820 Serbs who constituted 38.8 per cent. Would you agree that the percentage of Serbs was marginally less than that of Muslims? Would you agree with that, Mr. Neskovic? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Marginally less, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Teslic, the next-door municipality, on the other hand, had an overall majority which was Serb, didn't it? 55 per cent? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 2nd and 3rd of May of 1992, you were working, were you, as a prosecutor in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that night the town of Doboj was taken over, wasn't it, by the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Serb forces occupied all the municipal institutions, the SUP building, the municipality building. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Doboj saw some of the highest concentration of what I will paramilitary forces; that is to say, units of Arkan men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: How could I know that? I -- wait a minute. When you put a question to me, I have to respond. In the night of the 2nd to the 3rd of May, Doboj was taken over. Before the war, I worked in the prosecutors' office, and I returned to that position on the -- between the 10th and the 15th of May. Up till that time I stayed at home. I couldn't leave the house. Doboj was the front line. It was surrounded. It was full of refugees and full of different kinds of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am suggesting to you, sir, that before the actual takeover whilst you were still walking around the town, there could be seen there units of Arkan's men. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Seselj's White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- Martic's men? You're saying you never saw any of those either?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no Martic's men. When there was fighting around the corridor in June, that's when soldiers from the Knin Krajina and Bosnian Krajina arrived, and they were concentrated around Doboj. That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover, the declaration of a Serb crisis staff was made, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately after that crisis staff was declared, they became the government of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that was the municipal body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first thing that happened was that non-Serbs were dismissed from jobs. That's what happened as well, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In some places, they were dismissed; in other places, they continued working. And in yet other places, they failed to show up for work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you replaced, didn't you, as president of the Doboj court, a Muslim? That's right, isn't it, Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't understand your question. The president of the district court, the high court? The president of the high court in Doboj before me was a Croat, Kresimir Zubak who in early May left Doboj, and he was deputy prime minister of Herceg Bosna in Mostar. So his position remained vacant. There was never a Muslim president of the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're quite right. I'm sorry. He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: And nobody dismissed him. It was a vacant position. At that time, I was working in the prosecutors' office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you yourself, in fact, become a member of that crisis staff by virtue of your position?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely sure because members of the judiciary could not be members of the crisis staff. They could only be working on behalf of the municipality. There was a mistake in an interview where a witness told you that I had been a member of the crisis staff. But that was an error. It was not true. I was not a member of the crisis staff, nor could I attend their meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He seems to be very well informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know what a witness told us?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Because your investigator told me this. I was the liaison officer at the time. Are you talking about the statement of -- I can't say the name now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would be very grateful, sir, if you would not mention any names in open court. You're saying -- you were told when you were the liaison officer between the Republika Srpska and this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was finding witnesses for you. I brought witnesses here for you to interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that Jovo Rosic was a member of the regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that. It was published in the newspapers. I don't know how he could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may be a reasonable time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break of 20 minutes. Is that fine with the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see nodding. Let's try and cover as much ground as we can, and if necessary then we finish about five minutes earlier. We'll continue on Monday as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask if it will be Monday morning or Monday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't remember, Ms. Korner. I think it's in the morning on Monday, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Monday morning in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's in the morning. I am sending -- because there was a seesaw going on between me, my Trial Chamber, and Milosevic, so that we could accommodate the Milosevic trial to sit on Monday instead of us, and it had been on and off and on and off. So now I just sent a memo to Mr. Roberts to make sure that we have the courtroom available on Monday. Thank you. 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to carry on just for a few more minutes about conditions in Doboj after the takeover. It's right, isn't it, that during the course of May all the mosques in Doboj town, three of them, were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Catholic church was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm going to object because going into the events in Doboj is outside the parameters of this indictment, and I would suggest to the Court it's beyond the scope of the questioning that the Court undertook when this gentleman appeared before this Court. So I would object to any continued questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm dealing with these matters on -- from the point of view of investigation, prosecution, and the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand, because to be honest with you, I was going draw your attention that in summoning this witness we did not indicate these events as amongst those that he would be questioned by us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it did occur to me that the reason behind the question was what did he do at the time because he was prosecuting? So I will allow the question within those parameters, Mr. Cunningham. And that's why I didn't stop you actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wouldn't be asking. I appreciate it's outside the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, I put two and two together very quickly, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the destruction of the religious edifices, there were numerous detention facilities set up, weren't there? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a detention facilities in Doboj where people were held in custody when trials were pending, and there were others that the army controlled. But I don't know about those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bare ammunition warehouse. Or B-a-r-e, I'm not entirely sure of the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I have heard of that as being held by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Spreca prison, S-p-r-e-c-a, with an accent?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That is a detention unit in the Spreca prison, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you made aware that there were beatings and killings taking place in these facilities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not. However, I do know that the representatives of the military court and prosecution from Bijeljina worked in Doboj on some such cases in view of the fact that that came under their competency, if you're referring to May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody ever -- was any investigation carried out into the destruction of the three mosques and the Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that the military court conducted an investigation, and I don't remember at that time that the prosecutor's office did either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your court ever deal with anyone for the -- those criminal acts?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: My court dealt with appeals from the lower courts, for individual crimes such as murder perpetrated by civilians. So our court was in charge of individuals who were civilians. As to those who belonged to the armed forces, it was the military court that dealt with such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you deal with -- were there any prosecutions in your court for Serbs, civilians, who had killed non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. They were prosecuted for robbery, for armed robbery, and for killings, for murder. And our records -- the records were kept by the prosecutor. And if the crime could not be proved, it was documented and investigations conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say how many convictions of Serbs for killing non-Serbs there were whilst you were at -- president of the Doboj court?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. That's statistics now. Perhaps had I prepared for a question like that, I could have had the figures. And I can say that I think that certain individuals are still serving a prison sentence pursuant to convictions like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move, then, from Doboj to this question of your involvement with this Mice case. Now, I want to make sure I perfectly understand this. You heard that the Teslic investigating judge, Mr. Kovacevic, had sent the arrested persons to the prison in Banja Luka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The police from Banja Luka had transferred these individuals to the prison in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you're telling us now. And I'm going to suggest to you that's not true. From whom did you get the information?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The president of the court Kovacevic, that they had in fact been transferred to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Kovacevic said to you that without his knowledge, the Banja Luka police who had arrested these men had transferred them from Teslic to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: He said that the Banja Luka police had transferred the prisoners to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's not an answer to my question. Did he say this was without his knowledge or authority?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't, did he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't say that to me. He didn't say that. That's why I'm not mentioning that. He didn't say with or without his knowledge. All he said was the prisoners from Teslic have been transferred to the prison in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because what I suggest you have been giving this Court to understand is that it was the police who had taken it upon themselves to transfer these men to Banja Luka. That's not right, is it? And you know that's not right.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that that is not right. All I know is that the prisoners were transferred to Banja Luka, and that I received information from Kovacevic that the transference was conducted by the police from Teslic to Banja Luka, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That may well be right, but there is no conceivable way, is there, under the law of the Serbian Republic or the Bosnia-Herzegovina law that those prisoners could have been transferred without the order of the investigating judge? That is the situation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about any such order. If they were under the jurisdiction of the investigating judge, which they were, he had to know whether he issued an order for that not. Now, why he informed me about that, probably to inform me because he knew it belonged to the realm of the high court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. The law, as it then stood, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or what was called the Serbian Republic, only the investigating judge had the authority to order the transfer of a prisoner. That is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. He would determine detention and give this order. But technically speaking, it would be the police who transfers the individuals, not the judge himself. The police following orders from the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we finally got there. It was clear, wasn't it, that Mr. Kovacevic had ordered the police to transfer these men to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did -- sorry. Did he give you any reason why these men had been transferred to prison in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have in your file, don't you, some copies of letters that were published in the articles about this case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to you get them out, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The letter, first of all, from Mr. --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Which letter did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The letter first of all from Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Bjelosevic, the chief of the CSB in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one mentioned by the witness earlier on in -- yeah, okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just read, please, to the Court, slowly, so it can be translated, what that says. And the date, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I have copied this out from the newspapers on the 29th of September 1999. And I learned for the first time when I read it in the papers, and in my previous statement I've already said that the army and police went to the judge. "The Ministry of the Interior, the security service centre of Doboj, the 17th of July, to the investigating judge of the basic court in Teslic and the case of Culibrk Dobrivoje and others, their request to be released. And there are criminal proceedings against Culibrk Dobrivoje and others with the court for having perpetrated several criminal acts in the area bearing in mind" - I apologise for reading too fast - "bearing in mind that the broader area of Teslic and Tesanj has been engulfed by a war and conflict. As the conflict could expand we request that Culibrk Dobrivoje be released immediately, and as well as the others, Tekic Slobodan, Spaso Slobodan [phoen], Djuric Stojan [phoen], because we feel that their personal security is at risk because the conflict has flared up around Teslic. We think that the criminal proceedings can be carried on against these individuals, that there is no impediment to that, and they shall be convicted and given a sentence commensurable to the crime, and they will be able to defend themselves while at freedom." The head, Milosevic [as interpreted] signed it, and this was published on the 29th of September. And I photocopied this and left it in my archives, and I've already said that the police went to see the investigating judge to have these released. He did not comply with their request because they were released only on the 6th of August. So he followed requests from the army later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just correct, please, it was signed not by Milosevic but by Bjelosevic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Bjelosevic. Andrija Bjelosevic is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there was the letter from the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. And it is the letter to which I referred when I read out the findings of the investigating judge dated the 21st of June in which he says the release of military persons from detention to the basic court in Teslic, the investigating judge, the findings, and an investigative procedure is underway against this operative group, Ranko Sljuka, Sljivic Rodoljub, Gavranovic Sasa, the people involved, Kezunovic Dragomir, Mimic Ranko, Slavujic Dario, Sljuka Zoran and Devic Vitomir. "Bearing in mind that the above-mentioned were questioned, and in the Teslic/Tesanj area, there are combat activities going on. We request that these military persons be released immediately so that they could become involved in the war operations, and any prosecution against these individuals, if proof exists of them having committed a crime, can be conducted once the necessary conditions are fulfilled." And it is signed commander of the operative group, Milivoje Simic, and colonel is his rank. I've already read that out. And he did refer to that letter from the army, and that is why he released them on the 21st of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. The reason that Mr. Kova -- Judge Kovacevic sent those men to Banja Luka prison rather than prison in Doboj was because, wasn't it, that he was uncertain that they would be kept in prison as far as the police members were concerned?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these members of the police were released on the 6th of August. They were the only ones that stayed. So I assume that the operative group of Doboj belonged to the 1st Krajina area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that your telex to the Banja Luka court president the following day had nothing to do with these demands from the police and the military?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I met these requests for the first time -- I saw them in 1999 for the first time, and I photocopied them from the newspaper articles, and that's why I brought them here into court, to present them if the need arises. So it's pure coincidence that the 17th of July is the day on all three documents. And I checked that out to see why, but I wasn't able to see any connection between them. The 17th was a Friday, so because of the weekend, they wanted to do it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, I needn't have brought them into court, and I wouldn't have brought them in had I not been certain of what I just told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: But this is how it was. They were transferred on the 17th, so it is normal that this was written on the 17th, and that's when I learned about it. It would be very strange had they been transferred, for example, on the 10th and the date being the 17th for all these three documents, and then the question could have arisen as to why they all had the same date on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. What was your objection to these men remaining in prison in Banja Luka provided that the investigation was still being carried out by the authorised court at Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any objection to the court conducting an investigation, nor did I have any objection to their being or not being in detention. What I did object to was their being transferred to the prison in Banja Luka when it was the prison in Doboj that belonged to the Teslic area. If detainees were being transferred to the prison in Banja Luka, this would mean that we no longer needed a prison in Doboj, then we would not have a court in Doboj. Doboj would no longer be the regional centre. Those were my conclusions. So I did not want to allow prisoners to be transferred to another prison when we had a prison. Had I known what would later transpire, I wouldn't have asked for this. I wouldn't have written this letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Provided that the Teslic court continued its investigative function and provided you, as the appeal court in Doboj, was still seized of the matter, why did it matter that they were being kept in Banja Luka to be interviewed rather than in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: What talks are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not referring to talks. There must be a mistranslation. I asked you, and this is the last time I'm going to ask you, if the Teslic court retained its jurisdiction and if the Doboj court retained its jurisdiction, why did it matter where the perpetrators of crimes were kept in prison?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you, because pursuant to the law they had to be in the detention unit belonging to the high court. The high court was in Doboj. That was the court that had jurisdiction over Teslic. That's what mattered. There was no other motive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on. Why didn't you tell Mr. Kovacevic, who was the investigating judge in charge of the case, that you were going to send a telex to Mr. Rosic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was unable to inform him of this on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell him at the time when he told you that's where they were, that this was, in your view, illegal and that you were going to say they should be transferred back to Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Because he informed me the day before, and the day before I hadn't thought about this transfer. Afterwards, I looked through the regulations. I saw that this was illegal and decided to send a telex. I think Kovacevic did know about it, but I can't assert that. He alone can say whether that's so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you what you know he said because it was published in the newspaper. But at what stage did you decide that this was an illegal detention?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Who said it was illegal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just told us that detaining them in the Banja Luka prison was against the law. First of all, tell us what section of which law you say this was in breach of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: What I said was -- no, no. I didn't say that they had been illegally detained; I said that they had been detained in a detention unit that was not the legal one. I will read this to you now. "Decision on the basis of the organisation and the headquarters and areas covered by the regular courts, Official Gazette number 6, 12th to 17th of May, Article 7. The high court shall be established for regions, the high court in Banja Luka for the Autonomous Region of Krajina; the high court in Trebinje for the Serbian Autonomous Region of Herzegovina, the high court in Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just tell us the part that says that if somebody is in the jurisdiction of the high court in Doboj, they must be kept in the prison in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The high court in Doboj for the territory of the Serbian autonomous region of Northern Bosnia. Teslic belongs to Northern Bosnia. And as for the legal provisions, I don't have the one about the execution of sanctions of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted by Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look, I'm sorry. It's a simple question: What section of what law says that persons who have been arrested within the jurisdiction of Doboj high court must be imprisoned in the Doboj prison as opposed to any other?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: The law on the implementation of criminal sanctions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which you don't have with you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have it with me. It's the old law of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I only have the decision on the establishment of penal institutions, but it only refers to their establishment, nothing else. It's about the appointment of prison wardens and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you accept that by the Article 192 of the law of criminal -- on criminal procedure, anyone being investigated or charged with an offence for which the death penalty is prescribed has to be kept in custody?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me check. I think there is something about that. It's the old law, the law on criminal procedure. Oh, yes. It's paragraph 4. "If the crime in question is a crime for which an imprisonment of ten years can be handed down, under the law, or a more serious sentence and in view of the manner of perpetration the consequences and other circumstances, citizens might be disturbed to such an extent that detention is necessary for reasons of safety and security." So that the sentence has to be ten years or more, and also the general public has to be upset about this, and the judge decided that the reasons for the citizens being disturbed no longer existed. So there have to be two reasons. A sentence of at least ten years and the public should be disturbed about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may have given you the wrong article, but it's a simple question. If someone was being investigated for a crime which carried the death penalty, and it may be Article 191, it was mandatory --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is Article 191. And he has referred to paragraph 4 of that article and not to paragraph 1 which deals with crimes which carry the death penalty.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Thank you, Your Honour. You've obviously got it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 1, it is mandatory that people charged with offences which carry the death penalty must be kept in custody. Paragraph 1 of Article 191.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In Article 191, paragraph 1, that's what it says, but the investigating judge in Teslic did not refer to this article. He referred to paragraph 1 of article -- or rather, paragraph 2, influence on witnesses, and paragraph 4 which I read -- or rather, Article 4. If the prosecutor did not refer to that article, then the judge could not do so proprio motu. But I think that the death penalty was abolished at that point in time. I think there is a decision in May 1992 which says that the death penalty shall be abolished in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to spend too long on this. But it's right, isn't it, that there's no way that these men should have been released? You agree with that, don't you, in the light of the serious nature of the charges against them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: In peacetime conditions, they would never have been released. It's probably due to the war circumstances that they were released. Had this happened in peacetime, they would have been in detention until they were sentenced. I'm telling you this from my own experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to deal with the question of this telex. You sent this telex to Jovo Rosic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the minister of justice, and the warden of the district prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any other action to ensure that these men were released from Banja Luka prison?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No steps at all. I immediately archived this. I didn't know whether it would be followed through. I did this in order to show that the law had been broken. That's why I sent this to the ministry and to Jovo Rosic. And in Banja Luka, they decided about the manner of their transfer, and I learned about this later on, as I said. But you can talk to all of them. I didn't contact any of them after the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just... Just look at that telex for a moment, will you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it better be given a separate exhibit number, although it's part of the larger file. I think we've got up to -- what exhibit number are we up to? It is actually already part of Exhibit P1969. But can I have it made P1969.1 so that we've got it also separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer in that telex only to the article that you just read to us, I believe, saying that the high court in Doboj is constituted for the area of the Serbian Autonomous District of Northern Bosnia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer nowhere to any provision that says "because of that, they are not properly being detained in Banja Luka prison." In fact, all you do is make a proposal.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Excuse me. The paragraph before the last: "As the high court in Doboj also covers the area of the Serbian Municipality of Teslic and the seat of the prison in Doboj has been designated for the Teslic area..." So I did tell him why I wanted them to be in prison in Doboj, because that's what belongs to the Teslic area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You say -- and I accept, I'm not disputing, that Teslic came under the Doboj high court. But you don't say anywhere, do you, sir, that because they are -- because it comes under the jurisdiction of the Doboj high court their being held in Banja Luka is illegal? Do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. I wrote to him as a lawyer, not as a layman. I said: "Pursuant to the decision on the basis, the organisation, and the seats of the areas of the regular courts of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Article 7, paragraph 5, the high court in Doboj has been established to the SAO of Northern Bosnia which includes the Serbian Municipality of Teslic." So I gave him to understand quite clearly that Teslic belonged to the high court in Doboj. Further, I informed him that "As the high court in Doboj also covers the Serbian Municipality in Teslic and the seat of the court for Teslic is in Doboj, we propose that the persons be transferred," and so on and so forth. I think this was quite clear, and I hope that my colleague understood it because he acted on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, right. The last thing I want to deal with today is would you like to go to your own copy of the document and the sleeve that goes with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we actually have copies of this, and we have got copies for Mr. Cunningham and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have three minutes -- two minutes left, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may these be made P2731. Yes, for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a whole series of documents signed by the various people who were in Banja Luka prison and signed by yourself in which the various people who were imprisoned, the Mice, declared that they would report to the district prison in Doboj on the 20th of July? And you have signed it and dated it for the 18th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you waiting for a reply?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just acknowledge that these are documents signed by you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes. That's my signature. That's why I brought them here, to explain them to you. Last week in the archives of the district court I took out this letter of mine, and along with it were these statements which I brought as evidence that they were in prison. When they were transferred to prison, somebody from the prison informed me that they were asking to take a bath. I asked each of them for a guarantee that after taking a bath, they would immediately return to the prison, that they should sign this. And when they brought this, I signed it and put it in the archives as evidence that they had reported to prison and that if they didn't, they should have detention ordered. So this is evidence that they had been released in order to take a bath, and I had to keep this in the archives. And this is still in the archives of the district prison where they promised that they would immediately return to the prison after taking a bath because there was no water or electricity in Doboj. So they went to take a bath. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that may be an appropriate place to end for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I entirely agree with you, Ms. Korner. We will rise now, and we stand adjourned to Monday at 9.00. Which courtroom is it on Monday, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour may wish to give the warning to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Mr. Neskovic -- Courtroom I? III. We have to adjourn until Monday. According to our Rules, since you are still testifying, and I needn't explain this in any great detail, you are bound not to contact anyone or discuss with anyone the matters relating to your evidence here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a nice weekend, everybody. We'll meet Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
